name: cli-config
body:
`kalide config` manages kalide's user-level settings — a flat key-to-string-value map persisted in a per-user config file under the operating system's user config directory (macOS `~/Library/Application Support/kalide/`, Linux `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/kalide/` or `~/.config/kalide/`, Windows `%AppData%\kalide\`), modelled on `git config`. The file is shared by every deck and every working directory and is created (with its directory) on the first write. It has four subcommands:
- `kalide config get <key>` prints the value and exits 0 when the key is set; an unset key prints an error naming the key to stderr and exits non-zero.
- `kalide config set <key> <value>` writes the value into the user config file and exits 0.
- `kalide config unset <key>` removes the key when present; unsetting an absent key is a no-op success.
- `kalide config list` prints one `key=value` line per stored key (no output when none) and exits 0.
A missing or unknown subcommand, a missing `<key>`, or a `set` missing its `<value>` is a usage error (usage to stderr, non-zero exit, nothing written). The store's first defined key is `default-template-library` (default-template-library); other keys are free-form. The command is local-filesystem only: it never reaches the network.

AC:
- `kalide config set default-template-library ~/libs/deck-templates` writes an absolute path into the per-user config file, and `kalide config get default-template-library` prints that absolute path and exits 0;
- `kalide config get missing-key` exits non-zero with a message naming the key; `kalide config list` prints `default-template-library=<absolute path>` after the set, and prints nothing on a fresh config;
- `kalide config unset default-template-library` removes it and a following `get` exits non-zero; unsetting an absent key exits 0;
- `kalide config` with no subcommand, or `set` with no value, is a usage error and writes nothing.
